schemes.name: KZG (EIP-4844)
schemes.label: KZG
schemes.note: 48-byte proof, 50,000 gas via point_evaluation_precompile. Requires the Powers of Tau ceremony — 140,416 participants over 69 days. Any single honest participant ensures security.

schemes.name: Groth16
schemes.label: Groth16
schemes.note: Smallest on-chain SNARK (~128 bytes, ~220k gas). Per-circuit trusted setup: each new circuit requires its own ceremony. Common in zkML pipelines as the final SNARK wrapper.

schemes.name: PLONK
schemes.label: PLONK
schemes.note: Universal KZG SRS: one ceremony covers all circuits up to degree n. Proofs ~768 bytes, verification ~300k–500k gas. Separating setup from circuit design is a major practical advantage.

schemes.name: IPA / Pedersen
schemes.label: IPA
schemes.note: No trusted setup. Generators derived by hashing a public seed to curve points — anyone can verify independently. ~500–630 bytes per leaf opening. Multiproofs collapse across shared branches.

schemes.name: Merkle Patricia Trie
schemes.label: MPT
schemes.note: Hash-based, not a polynomial commitment — included as a reference baseline. Branch witnesses run 8–20 KB per account access (10–15 hexary trie nodes × ~500 B each). 10–20× larger than Verkle witnesses.

schemes.name: FRI-STARK
schemes.label: FRI
schemes.note: No trusted setup, conjectured post-quantum resistant. Proofs ~100 KB — direct L1 calldata cost (~1.6M gas) makes posting impractical. In practice wrapped in a SNARK (Groth16 or PLONK) before L1.
